title: Se suele + infinitivo: describir un patrón general

sections.content: Se suele + infinitive (it's usually / it's typically) is the impersonal way to state a general pattern or convention without naming who holds it -- exactly the tool needed to summarize how scholars typically define and describe a contested term like populism. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Se suele definir el populismo latinoamericano como un estilo político que apela directamente al "pueblo".
items.english: Latin American populism is usually defined as a political style that appeals directly to "the people."

items.spanish: Se suele señalar, entre las características típicas de estos movimientos, la centralidad de un líder carismático.
items.english: Among the typical characteristics of these movements, the centrality of a charismatic leader is usually pointed out.

items.spanish: No se suele encontrar un acuerdo completo sobre si el populismo debe entenderse como un estilo, una ideología o una estrategia electoral.
items.english: There usually isn't complete agreement about whether populism should be understood as a style, an ideology, or an electoral strategy.

items.spanish: Lo que sí se suele reconocer, casi sin excepción, es que estos movimientos surgieron en un contexto muy particular.
items.english: What is usually acknowledged, almost without exception, is that these movements arose in a very particular context.

sections.content: Se suele + infinitive is built from soler (to usually do something) plus the impersonal se -- don't confuse it with the simpler suele + infinitive, which needs a stated subject (el líder suele hablar por radio).
